allocation_status: Teaching design; no official count in the verified source.
rationale: Thirteen40minute lessons separate motion terms/graphs,three equation applications,piecewise reasoning,conditional actual low-drop investigation,frame evidence,up/down free fall,real-life implications and independent final. No derivations required;equations are applied with conditions. Actual observation/video/research provision remains explicit.
prerequisites: Signed numbers,units,ratios,squares/square roots and graph axes.
Distinguish position change,path length and ideal versus actual data.
teacher_confirmation_required: Approve soft light object,stable floor-level catch tray,clear exclusion zone and drop≤0.50m;no climbing,roads,stairs,windows or hard/heavy loads.
Actual release/observation/frame records need observed roles,date,height and conditions;supplied GSLM9 cannot certify investigation.
Do not claim human stopwatch timing of a low drop measures precise g;approved calibrated frame evidence needed for quantitative acceleration.
Use g10m/s² only as stated task approximation;actual local gravity/drag/measurement conditions differ.
Preserve road-contact versus gravity-only distinction despite source PCI linking road safety/free fall.
Approve actual digital/print sources and record navigation separately.
Confirm accessibility,pacing and any investigation setup needs.

lesson_map.title: How do distance and displacement differ?
What does a position-time graph show?
Does negative acceleration always mean slowing?
How is displacement calculated during acceleration?
What can an equation without time determine?
How can one trip need two models?
What can a safe low-drop investigation establish?
How do equal-time positions support a gravity model?
How are downward free-fall variables calculated?
What is acceleration at the highest point?
How do motion models support safer decisions?
Can motion evidence support an independent explanation?
